chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Walter Page's many instruments and the bands Jones listened to
summary: He recalls Page on baritone, tuba and bass, and says he heard Edwards Collegians, McKinney's and George E. Lee's band as a kid.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: He was my son and my father. He was the father of us all. See because when I first saw Mr. Walter Page I saw him with a baritone saxophone, I saw him with a tuba and a bass fiddle. He had the bass fiddle with a light in it. They used to do derby fans with -
Tuba with a light in it, you mean?

Yes. It had a light in it and he did a plus the fact derby fan in the tuba yet; they had bottles and they did 'Little Liza Jane' and they did it on bottles. It was when they had Lynch and, oh my God, I never heard it better. Lynch was a guitar player. I never heard a band. Now I had gone through - every year I tried to see Edwards Collegians, McKinney Cotton Pickers, and Fletcher Hendersons and all that - but they had no feeling, Milt. They didn't have that kind of feeling, notwithstanding Trent's band which was terrific, but remember I'm going to Eli Rice's band, I'm going to Grant 's band -
You mean you was listening to these bands?
You didn't play with these bands, did you?

No, no. I had no thought of playing with these bands. I would never thing of it. Me play with these bands? I'll go around the corner somewhere. Me play with these bands? 'You must be out of your mind!' See, they never saw a George Lee band, the most fabulous band that ever lived. Fess will tell you that. Fess will tell you, talk about dressing, ain't nobody dressed like George -
I didn't find out until I went out with Joe Bushkin what I knew about Fess. I've been there, you see. Because I was a kid, I was a kid that just wanted to be around you.
